answer: Stake bonds sized so faking does not pay. Each identity escrows 500 POA and gets nothing back until 3 auditors from a rotating pool of 240 countersign its work. Auditors take 12 reviews an hour, so 1,000 fakes need 3,000 signatures, roughly 250 auditor-hours, before the first credit lands. One dissent freezes that bond 30 days. A clean record stays ivory and releases at day 21 instead of 30, which is why the pool rotates and why an island of cloned identities costs 500,000 POA held for weeks on a network where 1M POA trades near 0.3 SOL. Terms are marble once the epoch record closes.
